data.name: TableTop Cricket
data.detailed_description:
Find the gaps in the field or just smack the ball out of the stadium, TableTop Cricket is a fast and furious take on cricket that takes you on a world tour with tense matches and challenges aplenty.

Includes:-
• World Tour - Compete as one of 16 countries taking part in over 60 challenges and matches.
• Versus Mode - Play against friends or go solo with multiple game types including T10, T20, ODI and Indoor Rules!
• Online - Challenge other players from around the world in a fast and furious Indoor Rules format game.
• Hall of Fame - Track your stats including runs scored, wickets taken even to how many times you have knocked over fielders!
• Play in homes from around the world such as Melbourne, London and Delhi with backdrops featuring play in a Kitchen, BBQ, Lounge or even in a Man Cave!
• Full Keyboard and Controller support - Take on your opponents using either a Keyboard or Controller, control everything from fielding set ups to batting and bowling.
• Try and unlock 12 Achievements ranging from winning a game online to scoring 10,000 runs.
• Unlock awesome trading cards just by playing the game. Then craft those trading cards into an exclusive badge to earn exclusive emoticons and profile backgrounds!
• Cloud save support - Save your progress at any time and any place and pick up right where you stopped no matter where you are.

Note: You must be connected to the internet to boot this game. You may disconnect from the internet once at the main menu.

reviews.review:
Now why am I reviewing this game 11 years after release? I realised it was on my wishlist for a while and will never be discounted again, so why not give it a shot. I used to have the physical tabletop game this is based off as a kid, so was hoping for a nostalgia hit.

It really does feel 11 years old. It looks like an Xbox 360 game that has been hastily ported, partly due to it running perpetually in 720p and partly because there are Xbox button references everywhere, despite me having no controller attached and playing on keyboard alone. The frame rate looks OK when looking at player animations, but the ball seems to run at 5fps and jiggles it's way down the pitch at you, making it difficult to time batting strokes right. There's a YouTube video in the community content showing it running at 60fps, but I have no idea how they made that happen. Stats tell me it is running at N/A, while GPU utilization is at 2% and CPU at 7% (which are the same stats as running idle without the game open). OS shortcuts don't want to work while playing, so can't pop up the start menu or window the game or even alt+f4 out of it. Esc not being tied to the pause menu is also super odd and coupled with the OS shortcuts being hobbled, made me think I was just stuck in game after starting a match. Tabbing out between innings caught me in a black screen with no way to get out short of task manager force close and obviously match progress is not saved.

Gameplay wise, I'm unsure if I was particularly suffering due to trying to play with keyboard. Everything is set up like you should be playing with a controller, there is no tutorial and you have to manually turn on hints if you want help beyond the button mapping in options. Batting is hit or miss, but bowling is just extremely difficult. When you move a player, it makes him shimmy 3 steps at a time and is completely imprecise, same goes for the bowling aim. You could never move your fielders in the middle of a delivery on the tabletop game, so I don't know why you can in this. That added layer just results in you jolting them about nowhere near the ball when you get the chance while fielding, but the AI will pounce on any ground ball that is within 5 metres of their fielder. Byes aren't counted as runs, as they were on the tabletop. LBW is never given even if blatant. One of the fun parts, naming your lineup, is not present, as all of the players are simply named after developers.

When I said the game would "never be discounted again", I gather from looking into the discussions there was a final sale many years ago on the developer website at half price. This page does not exist anymore and the game has not changed price for the last 2 years at least. The developer now works on the official yearly Cricket sim games and seems to have disavowed this game entirely on their own website.

Maybe this would have been worth it 11 years ago, but in 2026, I would heavily not recommend.
